drhp.business: Manufactures and trades carded, combed and compact combed cotton yarns (counts Ne 26 to Ne 40) and cotton bales at a semi-automated integrated spinning-and-ginning facility in Halvad, Morbi, Gujarat. Cotton bales are used both for captive yarn production and for sale to other spinning units; yarns serve knitting/weaving end-uses (denim, terry towels, shirting, sheeting, sweaters, socks, home and industrial textiles). Operates exclusively B2B, selling directly within Gujarat and, for out-of-state/export markets, through a reseller arrangement with 7 Seas Impex.
drhp.end_markets: Textile manufacturers, yarn exporters, bulk purchasers, fabric processors (B2B)|Denim, terry towels, shirting, sheeting, sweaters, socks, bottom wear, home textiles, industrial fabrics|Cotton seed to oil-extraction/animal-feed industries; cotton waste to non-woven/open-end yarn makers|Predominantly domestic (Gujarat direct; rest of India / exports via reseller 7 Seas Impex)
drhp.expansion: The principal growth step is the acquisition of Falcon Yarns Private Limited (a spinning company) funded from the Issue proceeds (Rs 11,151 lakhs part payment plus Rs 1,000 lakhs inter-corporate deposit for Falcon's working capital), which adds spinning capacity and scale to the existing 25,920-spindle / 7,700 MT yarn and 12,000 MT cotton-bale integrated facility at Halvad. The company has also built captive renewable power (solar + wind) to reduce operating costs.
drhp.mdna: Cotton bale (raw material) price exposure managed via order-linked hedging procurement and seasonal buffer stock|Seasonal ginning unit (~6-7 months, mid-Sept/Oct to March) driving inventory build-up|Customer concentration (top-10 customers 59.94% in FY2025) and supplier concentration (top-10 73.05% in FY2025)|Captive renewable power reducing electricity cost|Product mix between cotton yarn, cotton bales and by-products

business_ops.seasonality: Ginning unit operates seasonally (~6-7 months, mid-September/October to March, tied to the cotton harvest). Buffer cotton-bale stock is built during the peak harvest season (Oct-March) when availability is higher and prices lower, then drawn down in the off-season, driving inventory and working-capital seasonality.

supplier_concentration.note: Top-10 suppliers were 73.05% (FY25), 79.62% (FY24), 44.30% (FY23) of total purchases; >125 suppliers over 3 years, 6 of top-10 associated >5 years

business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Backward-integrated: an in-house ginning unit converts raw cotton into cotton bales (the principal raw material for spinning), providing raw-material security and by-product revenue (cotton seed, cotton waste). Ginning operates seasonally (~6-7 months, mid-Sept/Oct to March); shortfalls are met by sourcing bales from ginning mills/traders across Gujarat. Procurement is hedging-based (bales locked at order confirmation) with buffer stock built during the harvest season. Captive renewable power (1 MW rooftop solar, 4 MW ground solar, 2.7 MW wind) reduces power cost.

concerns_observed: The core use of proceeds is acquiring Falcon Yarns Private Limited at Rs 33.33/share - roughly 2.3x Falcon's own September-2024 buyback price of Rs 14.46/share - carrying valuation, integration and hidden-liability risk.
Single-facility and geographic concentration: all operations and most revenue are in Halvad, Morbi, Gujarat.
Customer and supplier concentration (top-10 customers up to 84.71%; top-10 suppliers up to 79.62%).
Heavy dependence on reseller 7 Seas Impex for out-of-state and export sales.
Cotton price/availability volatility and seasonal ginning driving working-capital intensity (inventory rose to Rs 16,531 lakh at Dec 31, 2025).
History of Companies Act/GST/Income-tax non-compliances and delayed filings (compounding applications filed; past non-appointment of internal auditor); executive team lacks listed-company experience.
Related-party dependence: promoter unsecured loans (recallable on demand), promoter-linked purchases and land purchases, and borrowings secured by promoter guarantees/property.
Rising leverage: total borrowings grew to Rs 10,147 lakh at Dec 31, 2025 (from Rs 8,101 lakh at FY2023).

red_flags: Falcon acquisition at ~2.3x its own recent buyback price (Rs 33.33 vs Rs 14.46), with promoters holding directorships on Falcon.
History of Companies Act non-compliances (compounding applications), Section 138 internal-auditor lapse, and GST/Income-tax delayed filings.
Related-party unsecured loans of Rs 472.44 lakh recallable on demand; borrowings secured by promoter guarantees/property.
Single manufacturing facility with no disclosed alternate arrangement, plus high customer/supplier concentration.
Negative cash flows reported in the past; rising total borrowings (Rs 10,147 lakh at Dec 31, 2025).
strengths_observed: Integrated spinning-and-ginning model providing cotton-bale (raw-material) security, by-product revenue (cotton seed, cotton waste) and margin control.

Strong profitability improvement: PAT rose from Rs 105.83 lakh (FY2023) to Rs 1,628.76 lakh (FY2024) to Rs 2,291.62 lakh (FY2025); EBITDA up from Rs 1,160.02 lakh to Rs 4,636.18 lakh; the DRHP claims the highest ROCE/RONW among selected peers in FY2025.
Captive renewable power (1 MW rooftop + 4 MW ground solar + 2.7 MW wind) reducing power cost.
Location advantage near Gujarat cotton-growing area with hedging-based, order-linked procurement.
SEBI-Listing-Regulations-compliant board (8 directors, 4 independent incl. 2 women) - stronger governance profile than a typical SME issuer.
Established customer/supplier base (>250 customers over 3 years; >125 suppliers).
